issues.description: Field and constructor parameter 'price' of class StockIngredient have inconsistent types across artifacts. The problem statement's UML and constructor signature declare price as int (StockIngredient(String, int, int)). The solution implementation uses an int price field and an int-typed constructor parameter (solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java). The template implementation, however, declares the price field and constructor parameter as double (template/src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java). This mismatch will confuse students: code that sums ingredient prices (e.g., SealSaloon.calculateTotalPrice) or assumes getPrice() returns int may produce compilation errors or require unwanted casts when the template's getPrice() returns double.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the price type consistent across all artifacts. Change the template StockIngredient to use int for the price field and constructor parameter and have getPrice() return int (public StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity) and public int getPrice()). Alternatively, if double is intended, update the problem statement and solution to use double everywhere and adjust code that sums prices accordingly. The simpler fix preserving the exercise intent is to update the template to int so it matches the UML and the solution.
